fields.Name: Salesforce
fields.Description: Salesforce REST connector: syncs CRM SObjects (Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, Case, Campaign, Task, Event, User) via SOQL watermark incremental sync; CRUD for most objects; custom __c discovered at runtime; OAuth2 JWT/Client Credentials.

universalPK.note: Every Salesforce SObject record carries an 18-character 'Id' field as its system primary key. Explicitly documented in Object Reference Ch1 ('Id: This field is unique within your organization') and used as the path parameter in all sObject Rows REST operations: GET /services/data/vXX.X/sobjects/{SObjectType}/{id}. Consistent across all 1,694 standard SObjects and all custom objects. Source: Object Reference PDF v67.0 Ch1 field properties; REST API PDF v67.0 Ch5 sObject Rows resource.

Configuration.AuthFlowNote: Salesforce supports multiple OAuth 2.0 flows. For server-to-server connectors the recommended flows are JWT Bearer (RFC 7523, no interactive login, long-lived org access) and Client Credentials (v55.0+, org-level access without user context). Web Server / Authorization Code flow is user-context only and not recommended for background connectors. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 Ch1 'Authorization Through External Client Apps or Connected Apps and OAuth 2.0'.
Configuration.AuthFlowAlternateNote: Client Credentials Flow (OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant) is available from API v55.0+. Provides org-level access without user context. Use when JWT Bearer is not available (no RSA key pair). Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 Ch1.
Configuration.AuthHeaderPatternSource: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 Ch1 line 527: 'HTTP Authorization — Provides the OAuth 2.0 access token to authorize your client. REST API supports the Bearer authentication type.' All cURL examples use: -H 'Authorization: Bearer access_token'.
Configuration.InstanceURLDiscoveryNote: The Salesforce instance URL (base URL for all REST calls, e.g. https://myorg.my.salesforce.com) is returned in the OAuth token response as 'instance_url'. It is NOT a static constant — it is org-specific and must be read from the token response at runtime. The connector reads instance_url from the token endpoint response and builds all /services/data/vXX.X/ paths relative to that base. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 Ch3 cURL Quick Start; SalesforceConnector.ts SalesforceAuthContext.InstanceUrl.
Configuration.TokenEndpointNote: LoginUrl is org-specific (https://login.salesforce.com for production, https://test.salesforce.com for sandboxes, or org My Domain URL). Token endpoint always at {LoginUrl}/services/oauth2/token. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 Ch3 cURL Quick Start example; SalesforceConnector.ts SalesforceCredentials.LoginUrl.
Configuration.TokenRefreshStrategyNote: Salesforce OAuth access tokens last approximately 2 hours by default (configurable in Connected App settings). The connector re-acquires a fresh token when the current token is within 20% of expiry or on a 401 response. No separate refresh_token grant is used for the JWT Bearer flow — the connector re-runs the JWT assertion exchange. Source: SalesforceConnector.ts TOKEN_LIFETIME_MS = 2*60*60*1000, TOKEN_REFRESH_THRESHOLD = 0.8.
Configuration.APIVersioningStrategyNote: API version is embedded in the URL path as /services/data/vXX.X/ (e.g. /services/data/v67.0/). Connector defaults to v61.0 (configurable per-connection via CompanyIntegration.Configuration.ApiVersion). Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 Ch1 URIs section line 492: 'https://MyDomainName.my.salesforce.com/services/data/vXX.X/resource/'.

PaginationDefaults.description: SOQL queries use cursor/query-locator pagination via the 'nextRecordsUrl' field in the response. When a query returns only part of the results, the response includes 'nextRecordsUrl' pointing to the next batch. The final batch omits 'nextRecordsUrl'. Batch size controlled via Sforce-Query-Options: batchSize header. Default batch size: 2000. Min: 200. Max: 2000. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 line 988-991.

Configuration.IncrementalSyncDescription: Two complementary incremental patterns documented: (1) SOQL watermark query: SELECT ... WHERE LastModifiedDate > {watermark} ORDER BY LastModifiedDate ASC — cursor-paginated via nextRecordsUrl. (2) sObject Get Updated endpoint: GET /services/data/vXX.X/sobjects/{SObjectType}/updated?start={ISO8601}&end={ISO8601} — returns a list of IDs for records modified in the window; records must be fetched separately. Watermark field: LastModifiedDate (or SystemModstamp as alternative). Get Deleted endpoint tracks tombstones. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 lines 2655-2680 (sObject Get Deleted/Updated) + Object Reference Ch1 system fields.
Configuration.WebhooksNote: Salesforce REST API does not expose traditional inbound webhooks. Salesforce provides Outbound Messages (SOAP-based) and Platform Events / Change Data Capture (streaming via CometD/SSE) for push notifications, but these are separate API families (Streaming API) requiring a persistent connection — not REST callbacks. The connector uses pull-based incremental sync. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 Ch5 'Gets subscriber information, and pushes notifications for streaming channels. See the Streaming API' (line 7408) — this references a separate Streaming API, not a REST webhook. Out of scope for this REST connector.
Configuration.BulkOperationsNote: Two bulk-related mechanisms documented: (1) Composite Batch: POST /services/data/vXX.X/composite/batch — executes up to 25 subrequests in a single HTTP request. Each subrequest counts against rate limits. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 line 5971 and 6960. (2) Bulk API 2.0: separate async API at /services/data/vXX.X/jobs/ingest and /jobs/query — designed for large-volume operations (millions of records), not per-record streaming. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 line 7073.
Configuration.CompositeAPIMaxSubrequestsSource: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 line 5971: 'Regular composite requests have a limit of 25 subrequests. Composite graphs increase this limit to 500.' Also line 6960: 'Executes up to 25 subrequests in a single request.' Also line 22737-22738: 'Executes up to 25 subrequests in a single request... Each subrequest counts against rate limits.'
Configuration.DiscoverObjectsMechanism: Runtime discovery via GET /services/data/vXX.X/sobjects/ (Describe Global endpoint). Returns JSON array of SObject descriptors including name, label, queryable, createable, updateable, deletable flags. Each accessible SObject is a potential Integration Object. Custom objects (__c suffix) and managed package objects (namespace__Name) appear here and are included in runtime discovery. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 Ch5 sObject Basic Information resource.
Configuration.DiscoverFieldsMechanism: Runtime discovery via GET /services/data/vXX.X/sobjects/{SObjectType}/describe (sObject Describe endpoint). Returns full field metadata: name, label, type, length, precision, scale, nillable, createable, updateable, filterable, sortable, defaultedOnCreate, idLookup, referenceTo (FK targets), and more. Custom fields have __c suffix. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 Ch5 sObject Describe resource.
Configuration.DiscoveryIsAuthoritativeRationale: The GET /services/data/vXX.X/sobjects/ (Describe Global) endpoint returns the COMPLETE credentialed gamut of SObjects accessible to the authenticated user — all standard, custom, and managed-package objects the org exposes. It is not a filtered subset. When this endpoint no longer returns an object, that object has been genuinely removed from (or is no longer accessible within) the org. Therefore a comprehensive refresh may safely deactivate objects that no longer appear. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 Ch5 sObject Basic Information resource — the endpoint enumerates ALL objects in the org-specific catalog. SOURCE_STUDY.md: 'Each accessible SObject is a potential Integration Object. Custom objects (__c suffix) and managed package objects (namespace__Name) appear here and are included in runtime discovery.'

ErrorResponseShape.description: Salesforce REST API error responses are JSON arrays. Each element in the array is an error object. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 lines 1196-1217 (Incorrect ID example and Resource doesn't exist example).

errorCode.description: Machine-readable error code (e.g. MALFORMED_ID, NOT_FOUND, REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, INVALID_FIELD).

fields.description: Field names involved in the error (present for field-level errors).

ErrorResponseShape.exampleIncorrectID: [{"fields":["Id"],"message":"Account ID: id value of incorrect type: 001900K0001pPuOAAU","errorCode":"MALFORMED_ID"}]

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: Salesforce REST API returns an ETag response header on sObject Rows (GET) requests — a hash of the content. If-Match and If-None-Match request headers allow conditional PATCH/GET operations. 412 Precondition Failed is returned when the ETag precondition is not satisfied. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 lines 805-820: 'The ETag header is a response header that is returned when you access the sObject Rows resource... used by the If-Match and If-None-Match request headers in subsequent requests to determine if the content has changed.' Also supports If-Modified-Since / If-Unmodified-Since time-based conditional headers (lines 841-858).
Configuration.DeleteSemanticsNote: Salesforce uses a soft-delete / Recycle Bin model. When a record is deleted via the REST API (DELETE /services/data/vXX.X/sobjects/{SObjectType}/{id}), it is moved to the Recycle Bin and its IsDeleted field becomes true. Deleted records are filtered out of standard SOQL queries but retrievable via queryAll. The sObject Get Deleted endpoint explicitly tracks deleted record IDs in a time window. Records can be undeleted. Hard delete (bypass Recycle Bin) is available via the Recycle Bin or admin operations. Source: Object Reference PDF v67.0 Ch1 line 2585: 'IsDeleted: Indicates whether the record has been moved to the Recycle Bin (true) or not (false).' REST API Developer Guide lines 2655-2657: 'Deleted records are written to a delete log (that is periodically purged)... filtered out of most operations... although QueryAll will include deleted records.'

WriteCapability.Note: Full CRUD supported for most standard SObjects. The REST API supports POST (create), PATCH (update), DELETE (delete) for SObjects that have those operations in their Supported Calls list. Some objects are read-only (e.g., User: no create in most editions; certain system objects). Per-object capability determined at runtime via the describe endpoint's createable/updateable/deletable flags. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 Ch5 sObject Rows resource; Object Reference PDF Ch6 per-object Supported Calls listings.

Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionRationale: Salesforce is a system-of-record CRM. Pull (read-only) is the safe default for any new EntityMap. Bidirectional sync against a live Salesforce org requires validation against a sandbox first — writes create or modify real CRM records (Accounts, Contacts, Opportunities, etc.) and incorrect field mappings or conflict resolution can corrupt customer data. The testing-agent refuses write tests without explicit allowWrite.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionRationale: Salesforce returns an ETag on every sObject Rows GET response, enabling true If-Match optimistic concurrency. LastModifiedDate is always populated and reliable, making MostRecent conflict resolution feasible when bidirectional sync is enabled. ConcurrencyControl=etag means MostRecent is safe to recommend (unlike connectors with ConcurrencyControl=none where MostRecent is not recommended because there is no reliable server-side timestamp for conflict ordering).
BidirectionalPreconditions: Validate all field mappings against a Salesforce Developer Edition org or full sandbox before enabling writes against a production org.
Confirm the integration user's Salesforce profile has Create/Edit/Delete permissions for the target objects.
Verify that required fields (e.g. Account.Name, Contact.LastName) are mapped — Salesforce returns REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING for any required field omitted on create.
Confirm conflict resolution strategy: MostRecent requires LastModifiedDate to be mapped; ETag-based If-Match requires connector to carry and re-submit the ETag on PATCH.

Test delete semantics: Salesforce soft-deletes to Recycle Bin — verify that the EntityMap's DeleteBehavior matches expectations (soft-delete is reversible; hard-delete is permanent after Recycle Bin purge).
Confirm the integration Connected App / External Client App has the appropriate OAuth scopes (api, full, or specific object scopes).
Configuration.CustomObjectMarkerPatternNote: In the Salesforce API, custom object names end with the suffix '__c'. For example, a custom object labeled 'Issue' in the UI becomes 'Issue__c' in the API. Managed package objects are prefixed with a namespace: 'namespace__ObjectName__c'. Source: Object Reference PDF v67.0 line 3128-3129: 'In the API, the names of custom objects include a suffix of two underscores followed by a lowercase c.'
Configuration.CustomFieldMarkerPatternNote: Custom fields use the same '__c' suffix convention. A custom field labeled 'Hire Date' becomes 'Hire_Date__c' in the API. Managed package custom fields: 'namespace__FieldName__c'. Source: Object Reference PDF v67.0 lines 3438-3440: 'In the API, the names of custom fields are identified by a suffix of two underscores immediately followed by a lowercase c character.'
Configuration.ManagedPackageNamespaceNote: Objects and fields from installed AppExchange managed packages carry a namespace prefix (up to 15 characters) separated by double underscores from the object/field name. E.g., 'battle__botId__c'. Namespace can be passed via the defaultNamespace client header to avoid prefixing in queries. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 lines 718-752.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: Clients consume the standard sObject CRUD/query surface. Bulk API 2.0 is an async, large-volume batch API designed for millions-of-records operations — it uses a distinct job-lifecycle model (ingest/query jobs), CSV-format payloads, and polling rather than per-record streaming. A future build can expand to it without re-discovering sObject metadata. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 line 7073; SOURCE_STUDY.md Out-of-Scope Families: 'Bulk API 2.0 — Separate API for large-volume batch; different endpoint structure; not sObject-per-record streaming'.

Clients consume the standard sObject CRUD/query surface. The Composite/Batch API is a call-multiplexing facility that wraps multiple sObject CRUD subrequests into a single HTTP call to reduce round-trips. It is not a separate data domain — the connector can optionally use composite/batch internally to batch writes, but the sync unit is still the per-sObject endpoint. This family is out of scope as a distinct sync target; composite endpoints may be used as an internal transport optimization. Source: REST API Developer Guide v67.0 Ch5 Composite resources; CompositeAPIMaxSubrequests=25 documented in BulkOperationsAvailable.

Clients consume the standard sObject CRUD/query surface for CRM business data. The Metadata API is a SOAP-based API for deploying org configuration artifacts (custom objects, layouts, workflows, code, validation rules) — it manages schema and process definitions, not CRM records. It uses SOAP envelopes, a deployment job model, and is entirely separate from the REST sObject surface. A future build can expand without re-discovering sObject metadata. Source: SOURCE_STUDY.md Out-of-Scope Families: 'Metadata API (SOAP) — Deploys org config (code, layouts, workflows); not CRM data; SOAP-based'.

Clients consume the standard sObject CRUD/query surface. The Tooling API is a developer/DevOps API for querying and managing Apex code, test coverage, debug logs, and development metadata. It is not CRM business data. Source: SOURCE_STUDY.md Out-of-Scope Families: 'Tooling API — Developer/DevOps API (Apex code, test execution); not CRM sync data'.

Clients consume the standard sObject CRUD/query surface. B2C Commerce (formerly Demandware) is a separate commerce platform with a distinct REST API, data model, and authentication scheme — it does not share the /services/data/vXX.X/sobjects/ endpoint structure of the Salesforce Platform REST API. A future build for the B2C Commerce API would be an entirely separate connector, not an extension of this one. Source: SOURCE_STUDY.md Out-of-Scope Families: 'B2C Commerce — Separate B2C Commerce platform with distinct API; not sObject REST'.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: Streaming API / Platform Events / Change Data Capture
OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: Clients consume the standard pull-based sObject CRUD/query surface. The Streaming API (CometD/SSE) provides push notifications via persistent connections and is a separate API family. The connector uses pull-based incremental sync (SOQL watermark + sObject Get Updated/Deleted) instead of a push/streaming model. Source: SOURCE_STUDY.md Out-of-Scope Families: 'Streaming / PushTopic / CDC — Event-push via CometD/SSE; pull-based connector uses GetUpdated/SOQL instead'.

Clients consume the standard sObject CRUD/query surface for CRM business data. The Connect API (Chatter) is a social/collaboration layer for feeds, groups, topics, and messages — not core CRM records. It uses distinct /connect/ endpoint paths. Source: SOURCE_STUDY.md Out-of-Scope Families: 'Connect / Chatter API — Social/collaboration layer; not core CRM data'.

Clients consume the standard sObject CRUD/query surface. CRM Analytics (Einstein Analytics) is a separate reporting/BI platform with its own API for datasets, lenses, dashboards, and recipes — not CRM record data. Source: SOURCE_STUDY.md Out-of-Scope Families: 'Analytics / Reports / Dashboards — Einstein Analytics separate API; reports are aggregations not raw records'.
